correctness.rationale: Direct weighted radial integration gives \(\|K_z\|_{p,\alpha}^p={}_2F_1(a,a;\beta;|z|^2)\). Euler transformation gives the exact normalized profile \((1-|z|^2)^c\|K_z\|_{p,\alpha}^p={}_2F_1(d,d;\beta;|z|^2)\). Gauss' boundary value gives the source sharp constant. For \(0<c<1\), the connection formula yields the dominant fractional branch with the displayed gamma coefficient; for \(c>1\), Gauss' formula applied to the derivative yields coefficient \(-d^2/(c-1)\); for \(c=1\), the derivative is zero-balanced and its logarithmic divergence integrates to \(-d^2s\log(1/s)\). The positive \(p\)-th root produces the stated norm coefficients, and \(p=2\) is exactly constant.

value.rationale: The normalized reproducing kernels are a central test family in the recent boundedness/compactness theorem. The lead source controls their norms only between two constants, while the older sharp theorem fixes only the limiting constant. The accepted theorem identifies the first nontrivial defect and shows that its regularity changes at the natural curve \((p-1)(\alpha+2)=1\), with a genuinely logarithmic resonance at equality and exact Hilbert cancellation at \(p=2\). This is a structural parameter phase of the kernel normalization rather than a routine numerical refinement.
